newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Nortel completes Vietnam telecoms upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Nortel completes Vietnam telecoms upgrade.

text.p: Canadian telecommunications company Northern Telecom Ltd (Nortel) said it has completed work on Vietnam's new high-capacity fibre optic telecoms trunk-route, the first in the ASEAN region.

Nortel said in a statement received by Reuters on Monday that the 3,000 km network had upgraded Vietnam's domestic and international telecoms capacity to allow video conferencing, remote database access and multimedia file transfers.
Work on the trunk-route was completed on Friday, it said.
The project was completed in conjunction with Vietnam Telecom National (VTM) and Telstra International in two phases.
Phase one, involving major cities between Hanoi in the north and Ho Chi Minh City in the south, was completed in March 1996. Phase two established services to rural and isolated areas.
In a separate statement, Nortel said it had started work on a fixed wireless access phone system for Ho Chi Minh City.
The system works by transmitting signals to radio sites around the city connected to a central controller, removing the need for cable to be laid at customers' premises.

Nortel said the system could cater for up to 100,000 users, cutting waiting lists for connections. The company said it expects 20,000 customers to have phone access through this system by the end of the year.
